edges.description: Drawn from the COG4 lesion rather than from the glycosylation defect, because the source treats the complex's autophagy role as separate from its role in glycosyltransferase localisation. Marked unknown-intermediates: nothing cited measures autophagic flux in COG4-deficient cells.

edges.target: Impaired Golgi Vesicle Tethering and Retrograde Transport

edges.description: Retrograde transport is how Golgi enzymes are returned to their correct cisternae, so a tethering defect mislocalises them.
edges.source: Impaired Golgi Vesicle Tethering and Retrograde Transport

edges.description: How a general glycosylation defect produces this particular organ pattern is not established, so the edge is drawn with unknown intermediates rather than given a mechanism the sources do not supply.

The link is a proposal in the cited source rather than a traced mechanism. No study cited here measures autophagic flux in a COG4-CDG patient or connects it to a febrile episode, so the intermediates are unknown.
The R729W line reproduces the glycosylation defect in a controlled isogenic background.
edges.limitations: Immortalised non-patient cell lines expressing tagged constructs, so they model the molecular lesion rather than the multisystem disease, and no tissue relevant to the neurological or hepatic phenotype is represented.
edges.source: Isogenic CRISPR COG4 R729W RPE1 and HEK293T cell lines

nodes.description: The COG complex has a role in autophagy that is separate from its role in glycosyltransferase localisation. The source proposes this as the route to episodic fever specifically, distinguishing it from the features attributed to the glycosylation defect. Recorded as a parallel branch rather than downstream of the glycosylation node for that reason.

evidence.reference_title: Hypothesis: determining phenotypic specificity facilitates understanding of pathophysiology in rare genetic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the COG complex was recently implicated in the autophagy pathway, as are more than half of the genes underlying disorders that present with episodic fever.

nodes.description: With retrograde recycling impaired, the glycosyltransferases and glycosidases that should be retained in specific cisternae are mislocalised. The consequence is a processing defect affecting terminal steps in particular, which is why the glycan abnormality is deficient galactosylation and sialylation rather than a failure to build the core.

This is the system that shows the two alleles produce different glycosylation defects, which is the experimental counterpart of this entry's lump/split argument against Saul-Wilson syndrome.

nodes.description: Biallelic COG4 variants reduce COG4 protein. Full complex formation is still achieved but at a lower level, so the lesion is quantitative rather than an absolute failure to assemble. Whether the loss also propagates to the expression or stability of the other lobe A subunits is contested and is deliberately not asserted here: PMID:19494034 reports that it does and PMID:21185756 reports that the other subunits are unaffected. The conflict is recorded in the cog4cdg_conflicting_subunit_effects discussion.
